title: Prepare a blot-transfer cassette and roll out trapped air
instruction: Hold the wet layers aligned, roll the trapped air out, then close the cassette.
context: Cassette preparation for wet laboratory transfer requires uniform contact across the working area. Voids interrupt that contact, so the operator braces the loose layers at their edge while moving a hand roller across the wet area under pressure. The task uses an inert full-size trainer for this manual operation.
setup: A fixed 139 × 106 mm ABS tray on a riser supports a 100 × 75 mm water-wetted PET contact face over compliant layers. Three visible air pockets at marked positions have diameters of 14, 16 and 14 mm. A 121 × 92 mm clear sliding lid starts at the 127 mm open stop. A loose brayer with a 106 mm wide, 28 mm diameter rubber drum and polymer grip rests beside the cassette in a two-seat open saddle. The README specifies the dimensions, locations and reset.
scoring: Award 0.25 for each of the three marked pockets absent in the after-rolling photo, up to 0.75. Award 1.0 when all three are absent, the layer edges finish within 3 mm of their registration marks, and the lid stays within 4 mm of its closed stop for at least 0.5 seconds. Score 0 if no pocket is cleared. Either arm may take each role.
reset_notes: Restore the sheet registration, three distinct visible pockets, open lid and brayer on its two seats. Use only the inert wet laminate.
fidelity: The rubber drum rotates on a free native axle. The loose layers compress and shear under contact, and the lid moves through a native slider. Loaded, aligned rolling clears visible gap witnesses through a reduced wet-interface model. The layers and water are represented by a spring-supported patch and aggregate air response.
scores: Demo: 1.0 after 484 actions. Dream-1: 0 after 540 actions.
